name: Compressed Yeast Bread
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: nearly a quart of warm water
ingredients.originalText: nearly a quart of warm water

instructions.text: Dissolve the yeast in a pint of lukewarm water
Stir into it enough flour to make a thick batter
Cover the bowl containing the batter or sponge with a thick folded cloth and set it in a warm place to rise
When the sponge is foamy and light in half an hour, stir into this sponge the salt dissolved in a little warm water
Add the rest of the flour and sufficient warm water to make the dough stiff enough to knead
Knead it from five to ten minutes
Divide it into loaves, knead again each loaf and put them into buttered baking tins
Cover them with a double thick cloth and set again in a warm place to rise twice their height
Bake the same as any bread

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Dissolve the yeast in a pint of lukewarm water
2. Stir into it enough flour to make a thick batter
3. Cover the bowl containing the batter or sponge with a thick folded cloth and set it in a warm place to rise
4. When the sponge is foamy and light in half an hour, stir into this sponge the salt dissolved in a little warm water
5. Add the rest of the flour and sufficient warm water to make the dough stiff enough to knead
6. Knead it from five to ten minutes
7. Divide it into loaves, knead again each loaf and put them into buttered baking tins
8. Cover them with a double thick cloth and set again in a warm place to rise twice their height
9. Bake the same as any bread
